question.text: Most of the hijackers were from this country, and one of their stated goals was for the United States to remove troops from this country.
question.answerHtml: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia [or al-Mamlakah al-Arabiyah as-Suudiyah]
question.clue: Abdul Aziz founded this modern country by defeating the British-backed Hussein bin Ali.

swap.leadin: This country was created after the United Nations passed a plan to partition Palestine at the end of 1947.
swap.text: Name this Jewish state that within 24 hours of its creation was invaded by Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, and Syria.
swap.clue: This nation's city of Beersheba is known as the "capital of the Negev".

question.leadin: Some Westernizing efforts in this country included educational reforms under the advisement of John Dewey and the Hat Law of 1925, which banned the use of the fez in favor of more Western-style hats.
question.text: Name this country which had its borders redefined in the Treaty of Lausanne. Soon after, this country moved its capital to Ankara, though its most populous city is Istanbul.
question.clue: A region in this modern-day country contained the city of Hattusa, home to a Bronze Age civilization that mastered ironworking and was ruled by Muwatalli II.

swap.leadin: Nuri al-Maliki tried to catch a shoe after it was thrown in protest of this war.
swap.text: Name this war protested by Muntadhar al-Zaidi, during which Saddam Hussein was executed in its namesake country.
swap.answerHtml: Iraq War [or Second Persian Gulf War; do not accept or prompt on “Persian Gulf War” alone]
swap.clue: A speech in front of a "Mission Accomplished" banner falsely celebrated the end of this war.

question.leadin: The Battle of Karbala occurred between the forces of one leader of this government, Yazid I ("yah-ZEED the first"), and the forces of Husayn ibn Ali ("hoo-SAYN ibn AH-lee").
question.text: Name this second Muslim caliphate which was founded by Muawiyah ("moo-AH-wee-yah"), succeeding the Rashidun ("RAH-shee-doon") caliphate. It was defeated by the later Abbasid caliphate at the Battle of the Zab River.
question.clue: Their main branch, which got a reputation for drunkenness, fell after Marwan II lost the Battle of Zab.

swap.leadin: This polity lost land along the Mediterranean coast to the Fatimids.
swap.text: Name this Muslim caliphate that succeeded the Umayyad. Its caliphs included Harun al-Rashid.
swap.clue: The Mamluks were created to help rule this empire after its capital was destroyed by Hulagu Khan.

question.leadin: An invasion plan during this war had its name changed after the British and the French couldn't agree on how to spell the word "Hamilcar."
question.text: Name this brief conflict. Lester Pearson received a Nobel Peace Prize for his work in ending it.
question.answerHtml: Suez Crisis [or Suez War; or Suez Canal Crisis; or Suez Canal War; or the Tripartite Aggression; or Second Arab-Israeli War]
question.clue: This conflict was the center of discussions at the Protocol of Sevres after which Charles Keightley initiated Operation Musketeer.

swap.text: This ruler's country got intervened in by France, the UK, and Israel in the 1956 Suez Crisis. The US and USSR rained on France's parade, indirectly helping this leader.
swap.clue: Despite the suspicions of Ibrahim Hadi this man helped form a coalition of junior officers under the leadership of Mohammed Naguib known as the Free Officers.

question.leadin: This group established the consecutive Bahri and Burji dynasties, which began after Aybak established a sultanate shortly before his murder by Shajar al-Durr.
question.text: Identify this military group that overthrew Turanshah and ended the Ayyubid dynasty after resisting Louis IX's crusade at the Battle of Fariskur.
question.answerHtml: Mamluks [or Mamelukes; despite the claims of Wikipedia, do not accept “Marmaduke,” who is a fictional dog and not a Muslim soldier]
question.clue: Barquq("bar-kuk")overthrew the last Kipchak ruler of these people and began their Circassian-dominated Burji ("bur-JEE") dynasty.

swap.text: The first coffeehouses were founded in this city, from which they spread rapidly throughout the Ottoman Empire and into Europe. Europeans mistakenly thought that steel with wavy patterns originated from this city.
swap.clue: It was later annexed into Alexander the Great's empire and lost importance when the government was moved north to Antioch.

question.leadin: Marwan II was defeated at the Battle of the Great Zab in a revolution named for this black-bannered dynasty.
question.text: Name this dynasty which claimed legitimacy due to their descent from one of Muhammad's uncles. Caliphs Al-Mansur and Harun al-Rashid were members of this dynasty which succeeded the Umayyads.
question.clue: It secured its power by winning the Battle of the Zab and defeating the Tang Dynasty at the battle of the Talas River.

swap.text: The Battle of Basian was part of Tamar's expansionist campaigns against an empire ruled by this dynasty. The vizier Nizam al-Mulk helped this dynasty's ruler Alp Arslan invade and subjugate Georgia in the late 11th century.
swap.clue: One offshoot of this dynastic group was the Sultanate of Rum.

question.leadin: Following the successful Battle of Yamana, this caliph oversaw the compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript.
question.text: Name this caliph whose ascension caused a schism between his supporters and those who supported a man reputedly addressed as "mawla" at Ghadir Khumm.
question.answerHtml: Abu Bakr [or Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq ‘Abdallāh bin Abī Quḥāfah]
question.clue: Lubaina, Zinnira, and Bilal were among the many slaves this man used his wealth to emancipate , and the rest of his money went to fund an expedition at Tabuk.

swap.leadin: Despite a rivalry with Uthman, this man sent his sons in a failed attempt to protect him from assassins.
swap.text: Name this man who later became the fourth Rashidun Caliph.
swap.clue: Some of this man's followers split off and formed the Kharijite sect following the battle of Siffin, which he fought against the man who would eventually replace him, Mu'awiya.

question.leadin: This man outlived his son, military commander Ibrahim Pasha, by only a few months.
question.text: Name this leader who fought the Ottomans in a war that was ended by the Convention of Kutahya. The Treaty of Balta Liman effectively ended this leader's cotton monopoly.
question.answerHtml: Muhammad Ali Pasha [or Mehmet Ali Pasha; prompt on Ali]
question.clue: This ruler's refusal to sign the Convention of London caused the Oriental Crisis.

swap.leadin: This uprising began in Jabalia Camp in December 1987 and ended in 1993.
swap.text: Name this Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation, which preceded a similar event in the early 21st century.
swap.clue: This event was partly sparked by people spraying "Six To One" in graffiti in response to an incident in which two militants attacked the Gibor camp in the Night of the Gliders.

question.text: This Lt. Colonel of the Israeli Defense Force led the operation and was its only Israeli casualty.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the life of William of Rubrouck.
swap.text: After returning from the court of Mongke Khan with a letter addressed to Louis, William settled down in this city and started lecturing about Christianity. Theobald V of Blois was one of the commanders to order the Massacre of Ayyadieh in this city, later conquered by Al-Ashraf Khalil.
swap.clue: The Knights Hospitallers relocated to Cyprus after the fall of this city in 1291.

question.leadin: Identify the following concerning massacres of indigenous peoples.
question.text: Over a thousands Assyrians fleeing Iraqi pogroms were slaughtered at this 1933 massacre, in which children were notably run over by armored cars. It ended only after the Chaldean Catholic Church intervened.

swap.leadin: This dynasty declined after a defeat at the Battle of Al-Mansurah, although they managed to hang on until the 15th century at Hisn Kayfa. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this dynasty which replaced the Fatimids.
swap.clue: This dynasty lost territory under al-Adil and al-Kamil, and was finally driven out of its chief territory following the Battle of al-Mansurah.
